facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October. He feels like he is running on fumes.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October.

facts.heading: Work burnout details
facts.content: Daniel works as a project manager at a logistics company. He feels he has been doing three people's jobs.
facts.evidence: I work as a project manager at a logistics company and I've been completely burnt out since October.

facts.heading: Work intrusion into personal time
facts.content: Daniel continues thinking about work even when not working. He stays at his desk answering messages late at night.
facts.evidence: Even when I'm not working, I'm thinking about work.

facts.heading: Poor sleep quality
facts.content: Daniel's sleep is terrible. He sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about 4 hours.

facts.heading: Nighttime waking and pain
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at 3 in the morning and cannot fall back asleep. His head hurts when he wakes up.
facts.evidence: I wake up at 3 in the morning and just can't fall back asleep. My head just hurts.

facts.heading: Sleep cycle anxiety
facts.content: Daniel calculates how little sleep he will get, which makes his sleep worse.
facts.evidence: Then I look at the clock and I do the math on how little sleep I'm gonna get, which makes it worse.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights. He lies until about 5 AM before getting up.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest. Then I lie until about 5 and get up and make tea.

facts.heading: Father's Parkinson's diagnosis
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: my father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's current condition
facts.content: Daniel's father's hands shake, he is slower, and he gets frustrated.
facts.evidence: His hands shake, he's slower, he gets frustrated.

facts.heading: Father's role as strong one
facts.content: Daniel's father is always being the strong one.
facts.evidence: he's always being the strong one.

facts.heading: Driving father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel is the one who drives his father to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks, it's about an hour each way.

facts.heading: Lack of shared support
facts.content: Daniel does not have anyone who shares the care for his father. His sister Hannah lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: Not really. My angry sister Hannah lives in Toronto, so all the care for our father falls of me.

facts.heading: Guilt about expressing needs
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for saying anything about his exhaustion. He does not say anything to anyone.
facts.evidence: Guilty for even saying it. He feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill. So I don't say anything to anyone.

facts.heading: GP visit results
facts.content: Daniel had blood tests which were all normal. The GP said it is stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She said it's stress and exhaustion.

facts.heading: GP advised no talking
facts.content: The GP said Daniel had no time to talk to someone.
facts.evidence: she said I hadn't got the time.

facts.heading: Girlfriend booked time
facts.content: Claire booked time with Daniel. She expressed that she was done watching him disappear.
facts.evidence: Claire. She said she was done watching me disappear.

facts.heading: Claire is patient
facts.content: Claire is very patient and makes tea for Daniel. She does not push Daniel to talk.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire is worried
facts.content: Daniel sees that Claire is worrying about herself too.
facts.evidence: But I can see she's worrying about her too.

facts.heading: Claire stopped asking
facts.content: Claire stopped asking if Daniel wanted to go away for the weekend. Daniel always said no.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.

facts.heading: Emails cause stress
facts.content: The emails are a source of stress for Daniel. He has to respond to 200 emails if he is away.
facts.evidence: The emails. And if I'm away I'll come back to 200 of them.

facts.heading: Rest has a price
facts.content: Daniel feels that even rest has a price. He cannot remember the last time he was properly off.
facts.evidence: So even rest has a price? I can't remember the last time I was properly off.

facts.heading: Ran for six years
facts.content: Daniel ran every Saturday morning for six years. He stopped about two months ago.
facts.evidence: I've done it for six years. I stopped about two months ago.

facts.heading: Legs feel like lead
facts.content: Daniel's legs feel like lead now. He has not gone back to running.
facts.evidence: My legs feel like lead. And I just never went back.

facts.heading: Lost part of self
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself. He describes running as the one time nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself. It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Peterson sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.
facts.evidence: he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Daniel answers emails
facts.content: Daniel answers every email from Peterson, even when he is not bad. Claire hates this.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm not bad. Claire hates it.

facts.heading: Fear of not answering
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that Peterson will think he is not committed if he does not answer.
facts.evidence: Dan, he'd think I wasn't committed.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: There is a restructuring this spring, and Daniel is afraid they will let him go.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring this spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Fear of relief feeling
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that if he is let go, Peterson will think part of him would be relieved.
facts.evidence: He'd think part of me would be relieved. I'd feel horrible about being relieved.

facts.heading: Moves apart from tiredness
facts.content: Daniel moves apart from tiredness and feels flat and irritable.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Slept at colleague
facts.content: Daniel slept at a colleague last week or nothing. He sat in the toilets for ten minutes.
facts.evidence: I slept at a colleague last week or nothing and went and sat in the toilets for ten minutes.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms during sleep
facts.content: When Daniel was in the toilet, his heart was going and his hands were shaking.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Past heart attack experience
facts.content: Daniel has experienced a heart attack a couple of times. Once it happened on a train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: A couple of times. Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform.

facts.heading: Fear of losing self
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that he is losing it. He is afraid of coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up, like, I don't know, coping.

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habit
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day. He drinks coffee because it makes things worse.
facts.evidence: I want about six cups a day. Coffee, probably.

facts.heading: Evening wine consumption
facts.content: Daniel has started having wine in the evenings to switch his head off. He drinks two to three glasses.
facts.evidence: And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Wine effect duration
facts.content: The wine helps for about an hour. Daniel notes that it is not helping.
facts.evidence: It works for an hour. I know it's not helping.

facts.heading: Feeling about wine
facts.content: Daniel feels easy about the wine. He notes that it feels like he is listing everything wrong with him.
facts.evidence: Easy. It feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me.

facts.heading: Relief from speaking out
facts.content: Daniel felt a bit of relief when saying what he was carrying. He did not realize he was carrying it.
facts.evidence: Strange. A bit of relief actually. Like putting it on bad, but I didn't realize I was carrying.

facts.heading: What he wants to put down
facts.content: Daniel thinks he wants to put down the nights. He believes he could cope with the rest if he could sleep.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep, I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Grandfather's behavior pattern
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather never complained about anything. He did not complain once.
facts.evidence: He never complained about anything. Not once. That's the same. Just get on with it.

facts.heading: Daniel's self-perception
facts.content: Daniel thinks he would be seen as weak by his grandfather. He thinks he is not weak but very tired.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here. That I'm not weak. Just very tired.

facts.heading: Willingness to try small step
facts.content: Daniel is willing to try something small between now and next week. He has little left.
facts.evidence: Depends how small. I haven't got much left.

facts.heading: Proposed evening routine
facts.content: Daniel suggested a fixed time in the evening to switch off his phone for 20 minutes.
facts.evidence: Very small. A fixed time in the evening when you switch off your phone, even for 20 minutes.

facts.heading: Proposed time for routine
facts.content: Daniel suggested half past nine perhaps for the routine.
facts.evidence: Yeah, half past nine perhaps.

facts.heading: Plan for tracking sleep
facts.content: Daniel offered to note how the night goes when he wakes up.
facts.evidence: I can do that. Right down when I wake up. If I wake up.

facts.heading: Current feeling after session
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after the session. He feels shaky after discussing everything.
facts.evidence: Tired, but lighter. It's normal to feel a bit shaky after saying all that.

facts.heading: Acknowledged difficulty speaking
facts.content: Daniel found it difficult to say something out loud.
facts.evidence: Very normal. It takes energy to say it loud loud.

facts.heading: Agreed to meet next week
facts.content: Daniel agreed to meet again the following week.
facts.evidence: Same time next week?
